subject: Autoscale overlay pricing and cooldown terms
messages:
From: Jason Lee <jason.lee@avacloud.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodai.com>
Cc: procurement@avacloud.ai
Date: 2027-04-11T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity — autoscale overlay / cooldown questions

Marcus — thanks again for the demo last week. We're close on the Dedicated commitment but procurement needs clarity on the 'autoscale overlay' (burst/burst-add-on) economics and operational behaviour before we sign. Two quick asks so we can move to legal: 

1) Describe the billing model for burst capacity at minute and hourly granularity. Our infra team wants to understand if we get charged per-minute spikes or if there's an hourly rounding.

2) What are the cooldown and exception rules? We've seen 'cooldown windows' in other contracts that can cause surprise charges. How long is the cooldown, and are there caps for sustained spikes due to product launches?

I've attached our 90-day traffic forecast (AvaCloud_RFP_traffic_forecast.xlsx). If you can provide a short addendum outline we can circulate to finance/legal.

Appreciate a pragmatic option that avoids penalizing legitimate product launches.

—Jason
AvaCloud — Head of Platform
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodai.com>
To: Jason Lee <jason.lee@avacloud.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodai.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — autoscale overlay / cooldown questions

Jason — great questions and thanks for the forecast. High-level options below (short, non-legal summary). I've attached a draft SLA addendum that maps to each option.

Option A — Predictable overlay (recommended)
- Reserve a Dedicated commit (e.g., 320 GPUs sustained).
- Add an "Autoscale Overlay" SKU that provides burst capacity billed per-minute but aggregated for billing on a 1-hour window (per-minute usage aggregated and rounded up to 1-hour buckets for surcharge calculations).
- Standard surcharge: 2.0x per-token-equivalent for overlay GPUs (applies to minutes that exceed commit).
- Cooldown: 30-minute sliding window. If spikes are short and return below commit within 30 minutes, charges apply only for the overage minutes.

Option B — Tiered burst slabs (better for launch events)
- 3 slabs for burst per month: 
  - First 500 GPU-hours: 1.6x surcharge
  - Next 1,000 GPU-hours: 1.9x surcharge
  - Above that: 2.2x surcharge
- Monthly smoothing: we apply a 95th-percentile smoothing to avoid charging short noisy spikes at the highest slab if overall monthly usage is within lower slab.
- Cooldown exception: one "launch window" per quarter (up to 8 hours) that is excluded from cooldown counting if pre-declared 72 hours ahead.

Option C — Minute-level true-burst (highest cost, lowest friction)
- Billed strictly per-minute at 2.5x; no smoothing; short spikes are exact but expensive.

Trade-offs & guarantees:
- Throughput SLOs for committed capacity are guaranteed by the Dedicated SLA in the addendum; overlay provides "best-effort" extra capacity with priority levels (we can pin higher priority for enterprise customers at higher surcharges).
- We can cap monthly overlay charges as a percent of committed spend (e.g., overlay charges capped at 30% of monthly committed rate) for contract-level protection.

Next steps: if AvaCloud prefers Option B we can propose a 12–24 month reserved commit discount in exchange for improved slab pricing. Monica and Rishi — flagging commercial trade-offs (discounts, cap levels).

Attaching Draft_SLA_Addendum_v2.pdf — I've highlighted the overlay clause and cooldown language.

—Marcus
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodai.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodai.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T14:42:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity — autoscale overlay / cooldown questions

Internal note: AvaCloud looks like a strategic regional customer (big ML infra surface). They asked about cooldown and launch exceptions. My quick take: be willing to trade a portion of margin for predictability — propose a capped slab + one launch window per quarter.

Commercial levers we can use:
- Extend commit term to 24–36 months for an additional 10–18% off committed rate.
- Offer the first-month overlay slab at discounted surcharge (1.4x) as a pilot.
- Add a monthly overlay cap equal to 25% of committed spend for the first 6 months.

Two questions for Rishi (can you confirm internal approval thresholds):
1) Approve a pilot discount (reduce first slab surcharge to 1.4x) for a 3-month pilot if they sign a 12-month commit?
2) Approve the 25% overlay-charge cap for the initial 6 months as a commercial concession?

—Monica
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodai.com>
To: Jason Lee <jason.lee@avacloud.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodai.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — autoscale overlay / cooldown questions

Jason — thanks for the clarity and Marcus/Monica for the options. To be explicit on the commercial terms we can offer AvaCloud as a counter-proposal: 

Counter-proposal (Pilot + Protection)
- Commit: 12-month Dedicated commit for 300 GPUs. Standard committed rate applies.
- Pilot burst overlay: first 90 days we apply the slabed model with these concessions:
  - First 500 GPU-hours/month @ 1.4x surcharge (pilot rate)
  - Next 1,000 GPU-hours/month @ 1.8x surcharge
  - Above that @ 2.1x surcharge
- Billing aggregation: per-minute metering aggregated to 1-hour billing buckets for surcharge math (no per-hour rounding that hides minute-level usage).
- Cooldown & launches: 30-minute sliding cooldown; one pre-declared launch window per quarter up to 8 hours exempt from cooldown counting. For unexpected prolonged incidents (3+ hours sustained over commit), charges apply but we review credits case-by-case; we will auto-credit any overlay charges that exceed 25% of committed spend in the pilot period.
- SLA addendum: committed throughput guaranteed; overlay is best-effort with optional higher priority lanes available for fixed fee.

If AvaCloud signs a 24–36 month commit we can harden the pricing to: first slab at 1.2x and increase the overlay cap to 30% of committed spend.

If that package looks OK we will send a concise commercial term sheet and a DocuSign pilot order.

—Rishi
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Jason Lee <jason.lee@avacloud.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodai.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodai.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T16:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — autoscale overlay / cooldown questions

Thanks — that counter-proposal is exactly the granularity we needed. Two small requests before we send to legal: 
1) Can you add a 7-day notice requirement for the quarterly launch exception (we can do 72 hours or 7 days; 7 days is preferable operationally).
2) Please include an example billing line in the addendum showing how a mixed-minute spike maps to the slab math (we will share a sample spike from our forecast to test).

Agree to pilot. Please send the term sheet + DocuSign and we'll route it.

—Jason
Head of Platform, AvaCloud
